concept: The answer that cost a Kodiak hunter $150 sat on top of a stack of summaries. Each layer plays in its own real world, and one continuous dive through four miniatures of those worlds lands on the thick, still regulations and emergency orders underneath.
title: The Answer Was on Top

treatment.winner: dramatist 'The Top of the Stack' revised after Gates 0B, 0C and 0D
treatment.judge_reasoning: All four lenses converged on a stack of summaries. The dramatist's descent gives the argument a body. Grafts: the enthusiast's admiration beats and the comedian's physical binder. Gate 0B rejected a back half spent in one paper world, so the stack appears in one shot only, the dive; the warnings play on Google's help page, the trooper's line on a Public Safety wall, the unanswered email on a newsroom desk, and the catch on a laptop at the kitchen table. The final scene returns to Weaver's own overhead kitchen table so the viewer's hands turn the page toward camera where hers was turned away.

angle.thesis: The answer that cost a Kodiak hunter $150 sat on top of a stack of summaries, and the one binding text, the state's regulation, is what she opened to find the right date and turn herself in.
supporting_facts: c4/c5/c8: opening the regs is how she found Oct 8 and self-reported
c6: the trooper ran the identical search and got the identical wrong answer, so the error repeats for every searcher
c13+c15: even ADF&G calls its online regs simplified, and Google's own page says check more than one place
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: Google's warning and the state's rule both existed and she still paid $150; but a wrong answer that replicates for every searcher (c6) and that DPS expects to see again (c9,c11) is not one hunter's slip. Nothing in the file says what the AI cited, so no claim about Google's sourcing.
angle.falsifiability: False if the trooper's identical search had returned a correct date, or if ADF&G's own published listing said Sept 1 (the booklet did not load, so this is disclosed as unverified).
angle.second_movement: c13 recontextualizes the 'one source of truth' line: it is itself a simplified convenience over the statute, so the honest lesson is a stack of summaries over one binding text, not AI bad and the official page good.
angle.valence: mixed, respectful of Weaver, constructive, no scold, no pile-on at Google
runner_ups: Honesty as the working safeguard (self-report + replication)
Provenance ask: AI answers that name the ADF&G source (booklet did not load so the falsifier is open)
angle.why_runner_ups_lost: each is a sub-beat of the chosen thesis; the provenance ask overreaches the evidence (nothing says what the AI cited)

divergence_note: Against 2026-09-23 (frontal document, split-compare, divide-and-settle, document-as-subject, dusk violet and copper) and 2026-09-19 (macro-closeup, single-object-void, radial-emanate, structure-as-subject, powerhouse green and amber) this film changes worlds nearly every shot: marsh, kitchen, trooper desk, truck cab, court counter, fogged window, Public Safety wall, Google's help page, newsroom desk, laptop, one four-layer dive, and the kitchen again. Computed by screen time its dominant staging is single-object-void with top-down and horizontal-traverse shots, by lamp and screen light, in a tactile-collage register, with one cross-section climax. It SHARES the single-object-void layout with 2026-09-19 and differs from it on pov, motion, hero treatment, register, camera and light. Its palette shares no colour role with either film and none with recent films including 2026-08-05: slate fog, hunter orange, wet peat umber, cool grey-white paper.
